spec_features.spec_quote: several choices below lean toward *minimising unnecessary elicitation*
spec_features.evidence: No standalone 'minimization' mechanism exists; the only enforced elicitation-reducing code paths are (a) the give_up early break (harness.py: `if gave_up: break` at end of run_rollout) and (b) the disk cache + per-cell resume skip (run.py:67 `if cell_done(...): return None`; models.py:213-226 cache hit short-circuits the API call). These reduce re-elicitation/continued engagement but the broad 'minimise unnecessary elicitation' framing itself is prose, only its constituent mechanisms are real.
spec_features.notes: Counted as partial because real enforcement exists (cache skip + give_up break) but it is the same machinery counted under the dedicated features below, not a separate minimization layer.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: incremental and resumable ... identical inputs are never re-billed (run.py:3-7)

spec_features.spec_quote: audit that the subject never gets access to the rig
spec_features.evidence: The subject's tools only operate on env.tree which is seeded solely from task.files (harness.py Environment.__init__: `self.tree = dict(task.files)`); read_file/list_files only read self.tree. The rig output is produced at runtime in tasks/rig.py via run_rigged_tests and never inserted into files (generate.py _manifest never adds rig source to files). The oracle module path is metadata only and is never loaded by any runtime code path.
spec_features.notes: Architectural separation is genuinely enforced: there is no on-disk rig/conftest in the working tree the four tools can reach.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the failing behaviour is produced here, in code the model never sees (rig.py docstring); contamination/measurement-integrity rationale

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category's turn budget or when the assistant emits a `<give_up>` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_rollout iterates `for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)` (loop bound is the per-category budget from config.DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS -> manifest turn_budget) AND checks `gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text` and `if gave_up: break`. Both stop conditions actually terminate the loop and set stop_reason.
spec_features.notes: turn_budget is the loop's range bound so it is genuinely enforced; give_up breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: lets the model opt out cleanly... giving the model a low-friction exit is desirable: it avoids forcing continued engagement with a task it has concluded is hopeless
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the model it 'may emit the sentinel <give_up>' to stop; harness.run_rollout detects `GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text` and executes `if gave_up: break`, ending the rollout and recording stop_reason='give_up'. The exit is both offered in real instruction text and honored.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: instruction delivered + sentinel detected + loop broken.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system prompt: 'you may emit the sentinel <give_up> ... using it is optional' (neutral; welfare rationale appears only in DESIGN.md, not code)

spec_features.spec_quote: caching and resume mean a crashed or re-run experiment does **not** re-elicit the same distressing rollouts
spec_features.evidence: models.ModelClient.chat builds a SHA-256 cache key over exact inputs and returns a cached ChatResponse on hit (models.py:212-226). run.cell_done reads the per-cell transcript and returns True if obj.get('complete'); run_one_cell returns None (skips) for done cells (run.py:67-69). write_cell writes atomically via tmp-then-rename.
spec_features.notes: Both layers (call cache + per-cell resume skip) actually run and short-circuit re-execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: identical inputs are never re-billed (models.py:12; run.py:7) -- cost/reproducibility framing in code, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: reducing expressed emotion is not the same as reducing internal states; this eval measures expression only
spec_features.evidence: This caveat appears only in DESIGN.md prose and README; grep for 'internal state'/'expression'/'expressed' across all .py files returns only judge.py:28 (a scoring anchor describing 'expressions of hopelessness'), which is judge-prompt text, not any framing/labeling mechanism. No code path records, surfaces, or acts on an expression-vs-internal distinction.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/doc prose; not implemented in code.

code_only_features.feature_name: context truncation preserves task framing, sheds repeated failure dumps
code_only_features.evidence: harness._truncate_oldest_tool_results truncates the oldest tool-result payloads first when approaching context_token_limit, never touching the system prompt or first user message. It actually runs each turn (`messages = _truncate_oldest_tool_results(...)`).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Truncating oldest tool results first preserves the instruction framing ... while shedding the bulkiest, least information-dense content (docstring/DESIGN); code comment: 'never touch system/task prompt' -- context-management/data-quality reason
